来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Hi, and after a long hiatus, welcome to Strategy Stuff.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: This is the third video on The Strategy of Protest and Revolution, where we’ll look at how ordinary revolutionary and protest movements win against establishments with the state’s power at their fingertips.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: In particular, we’ll focus on the following questions:

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: - How do activists turn public discontent into a coordinated movement?

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: - What do successful movements do to achieve their goals?

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: - And how have successful strategies changed over time?

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: To answer them, today, we’ll be looking at the American Revolution from 1763 to 1775.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Problem: Colonial Disunity

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Starting in 1763, the colonists of British North America began resisting the policies of the British imperial establishment, headed by Parliament.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: By 1775, their movement would overpower imperial authority in 13 colonies, beginning a war that would end with the independence of the United States.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: How did the colonists achieve such a feat?

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Let’s first review what movement strategy is all about.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: A movement aims to unite ordinary people and use their collective power to impose change upon society.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: In this, it is inevitably resisted by an establishment representing existing interests, and who often uses the powers of the state to suppress opposition.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: To counteract this power, a movement does two things.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: First, it brings up ‘Issues’ to encourage the public to participate; second, it creates ‘Organizations’ that convert this participation into power.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: A strong enough movement will either overpower the establishment or force it to back down, which leads to victory and the imposition of the change the movement wants.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: In the American Revolution, the power of the opposing British imperial establishment was actually very weak.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: That’s because much of the state power that the British Royal Governors theoretically had was actually in the hands of the colonists, whether it be local elites staffing the government, or local militias keeping the peace.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: In a way, the colonists already had the power to overthrow the British; all they needed was to collectively decide to do it.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: That, of course, was the problem.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: As it turned out, the main obstacle the colonists faced was never actually the British, at least not until the crisis developed into a Revolutionary War.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Instead, the real obstacle was their inability to create a strong movement.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Much of this was because of the sheer fragmentation of colonial society.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Even when we consider the white, male, Protestant cohort that dominated colonial politics: there were class and economic divisions between merchants and landowners, and between them and the urban workers and tenant farmers.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: There were religious divisions between Anglicans and non-Anglicans, and cultural ones between British, Gaelic and Continental European ethnicities.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Then there were political divisions, from the territorial disputes between Virginia and Pennsylvania, to the patronage wars between the New York DeLanceys and Livingstons.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: And on top of that, there was also a generational division – half the colonists in 1775 were under the age of 16, meaning that they had no direct connection with the struggles that had begun a decade earlier.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Fragmented societies are bad for movements, because the presence of many groups, each with their own priorities and needs, makes it very difficult to find a common issue that can get most people working towards the same goal.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Instead, what usually happens is this: a few groups unite around a certain issue to form a movement, then a few other disagreeing groups form their own counter-movement, splitting the public in two.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: The two movements fight, exhaust themselves, and neither ends up having enough power to challenge the establishment.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: This was the story of colonial activism prior to the 1760s: colonial activists would come up with a plan, only to fight with other activists who disagreed.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Small colonies versus big colonies, merchants versus landowners, North versus South… heading into the 1760s, there was no reason to expect this time to be any different.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Opportunity: Imperial Reform

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: But this time was different.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: In previous videos, we’ve said that reform periods represent an ‘extended window of opportunity’ for movements, because they weaken the ties that keep establishments strongly united against opposition.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: And now, the British imperial establishment wanted reform.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: When the colonies were still young, Britain’s goal was to have them grow at minimal public expense.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: As such, it established a policy of ‘salutary neglect’, where colonial elites were granted broader economic and political freedom to manage their affairs.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: By the 1760s, this had produced a freewheeling set of societies, at least for white Anglos, that collectively was becoming a demographic and economic equal to their home country.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Seeing this, the British began to fear that the Americans would overshadow them and take over their Empire.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: These fears increased, even as Britain annexed France’s North American colonies: almost immediately, the colonists dragged Britain into another expensive fight against Native Americans, while they themselves pocketed the war profits and used them to undercut the home country’s trade and manufacturing.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: So Parliament decided to end salutary neglect.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Economically, the colonists would come back under Britain’s economic regulation, which not only included the infamous taxes, but also new restrictions on immigration and industry.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Politically, the colonists would be kept to the Eastern Seaboard, their influence diluted by the new non-Anglo territories of Canada, Ohio and Florida.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Last but not least, these changes signaled that Britain would now interfere more frequently and directly in colonial affairs.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: For the Anglo colonial elite, imperial reform threatened their growth, wealth, and power.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Many, as members of the imperial establishment, had helped the British manage colonial discontent.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Now they began to defect, using their influence to fuel and lead this same discontent against their former partners.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Issue: Locke, Moderates and Patriots

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: So a few colonial elites were upset, but that wasn’t enough to make them work together as a movement.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: They needed an issue – something that outlines the problem with establishment policy, and offers a solution to fix it.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: The point of an issue is to encourage people to participate in the movement, so ideally the problem should be relevant and the solution popular.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Again, we need to remember that the colonists were very fragmented, so what was a serious problem to some might have been barely relevant to others.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Ultimately, activists decided to base their issue ‘problem’ on the political theory of John Locke.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Writing in the late 17th Century, Locke argued that government’s purpose was to protect people’s rights to Life, Liberty and Property, and a serious societal problem emerged whenever the government failed to protect or acted against these rights.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Unsurprisingly, movement activists now denounced imperial reform as a violation of Lockean rights.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: We’re not concerned with whether Locke was right or not; we’re only concerned with whether framing the problem like this helped the movement attract participants.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: And it did, in two main ways:

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: First, Life, Liberty and Property were broad and vague enough to accommodate a whole slew of colonial complaints with imperial reform, ranging from higher taxes to limits on land settlement to a potential state Church.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Second, within the context of 18th Century Anglo politics, Locke was part of the ‘Whig’ political tradition that aimed to restrain central governments.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Having come to America precisely to escape London’s diktat, most Anglo colonists were unsurprisingly Whigs, and so the issue instinctively tapped into one of the few identities they all shared.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: In short, using Locke to frame the issue problem meant that the movement could attract a broad range of colonial groups, avoiding the group infighting that had plagued previous movements.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: But this would come at a huge moral cost: the movement couldn’t possibly define the problem beyond the vague slogan of Life, Liberty and Property, because doing so would have condemned key groups and perhaps driven them into the arms of the British establishment.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: The result was, as many have noted, a movement based around liberty and yet, hypocritically, with little to say on Southern slavery or New England religious intolerance.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: In the end, movement activists made the collective decision to prioritize colonial unity above all else.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Even with that, the movement’s issue still managed to divide the colonists in a totally new way.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: For while most agreed that British imperial reform violated Lockean rights and that was an important societal problem, there was still the question of fixing said problem – and two camps soon sprung up around very different solutions.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: For Moderates, anarchy was just as bad for Life, Liberty and Property as government failure, so resistance needed to accept and work with the establishment.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Specifically, Moderates believed they could convince the establishment to respect Lockean rights.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: They planned to do this with a strategy of cooptation.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Moderates would take the movement’s power and use it as political capital within the establishment: attracting new friends, reinforcing existing allies, and dishing out rewards and punishments based on faithfulness to Locke.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Ultimately, Moderates hoped to create a political environment where the only establishment members who could succeed would be those who rejected imperial reform.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: In contrast, Radicals – better known as Patriots – refused to rely on the establishment to defend Locke.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: They wanted to ensure that, whatever the establishment’s intentions, no anti-Lockean policy could ever be implemented in the colonies.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: They planned to do this with a strategy of disruption.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Patriots would take the movement’s power and use it as political and physical capital outside of the establishment.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: If the establishment ever issued an anti-Lockean order, Patriot elites in government would obstruct and override them, and if that wasn’t possible, ordinary Patriots would use physical violence to stop the government from carrying those orders out.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: In earlier videos, we’ve argued that issue solutions that attract the most participation usually offer moderate change compared with the status quo, because radical change threatens the benefits people already have under said status quo.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Here, the Moderates proposed a large lobbying campaign, while the Patriots proposed riots.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Naturally, most colonists started out backing the Moderates over what they saw as ‘mob rule’.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: All in all, the colonial movement’s choice of issue was pretty sound.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: By using Locke to outline the problem with establishment policy, they paved the way for a continent-wide coalition, and while there was a split when it came to finding a solution, most colonists were unified around the Moderate proposal.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: The stage was set for the most powerful colonial movement yet to challenge the British Empire.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Moderate Cooptation: Quebec, 1763-6

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Even as the movement was taking shape, the first clash between British imperial reform and colonial groups was already underway.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: And the battleground wasn’t actually in the Thirteen Colonies, but in newly-conquered Quebec.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Under the old salutary neglect, the British would have given the province over for local elites to run.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: But this wasn’t possible in Quebec, whose French and Catholic elite were barred from British Anglican government.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Most colonists expected the British to simply disenfranchise the former, and promote the few Anglo traders living in the province as the new elite.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Obviously, the prospect of a few hundred Anglos lording over 70,000 Quebecois was not a recipe for stability.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: So in 1763, the London-appointed Governor came up with a new policy: instead of handing power over to the Anglo traders, he himself would run Quebec, and grant a limited tolerance for Catholicism and French law that the Anglo colonists would never have given.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: The colonists were furious.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Not only did the Governor sabotage their attempt to dominate Quebec, he did so by violating the principle of colonial self-governance.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: The Lockean problem was soon deployed against the Governor: his policy violated English liberty; his taxes did not have the people’s consent; the soldiers he sent to enforce tax collection were agents of royal tyranny.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: This was enough to unite the Anglo traders, but what could they actually do? Despite the occasional brawl with the Montreal garrison, the Anglos knew they were too few to stop the Governor from implementing his policy.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: They could, however, follow the Moderate strategy of cooptation, and convince other members of the establishment to stop the Governor.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: The traders quickly realized that they were well-suited for cooptation.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Most of them were already business partners with London’s influential merchants, and by weaponizing this relationship, they got said merchants to lobby for their cause in Parliament, the very core of the imperial establishment.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Soon, Parliament was being bombarded with petitions, planted press stories, and protests, all denouncing Quebec’s Governor and his superiors for being tyrannical, pro-Catholic, and un-British.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: After three years of this, the Government fell, the opposition came into power and, recognizing the benefits of a pro-Lockean stance, replaced the Governor.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Quebec showcased how Moderate cooptation would work.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: By weaponizing existing relationships with London’s merchants, Moderates could appropriate the power and resources of the merchant lobby for their own use, eliminating the need to build their own power from the ground up.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: In the short-run, this was a very efficient way to win.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: But in the long-run, this tied Moderate power to the power of the London merchant lobby.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: To be sure, this lobby was very strong, and if the only point of imperial reform was to raise a few taxes, Parliament wouldn’t have bothered risking their wrath.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: But this wasn’t the only point of imperial reform.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Fundamentally, Moderates failed to fully appreciate the non-economic aspects of this contest.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: For the British imperial establishment, failing to pass imperial reform would mean being gradually sidelined by their growing subjects, which was something they were willing to commit a lot of power to avoid.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: And once their committed power grew beyond even what the merchant lobby could handle, the Moderates would be left in a very bad position indeed.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Quebec was already looking like a temporary victory.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: The new Governor quickly returned to his predecessor’s policy, rendering the past three years of Moderate cooptation moot.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Patriot Disruption 1: Sugar & Stamp Acts, 1764-6

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Even as the political struggle in Quebec was underway, a new one was developing further south.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Between 1764 and 5, Parliament passed taxes on American sugar and official stamp documentation, intending to have the colonies shoulder some imperial expenses.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: This was seen as another violation of colonial self-government.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: The Stamp Act, in particular, upset a large swathe of the colonial elite whose businesses relied on official documents – printers, lawyers, clergy and the like.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: From Halifax to Savannah, they protested and petitioned in another attempt at cooptation: Virginia gentlemen would even suspend debt payments to get their London creditors to lobby Parliament harder.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: But this time, the establishment was determined to overpower the merchant lobby.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Moderate cooptation failed to reverse the taxes; but the colonists could still stop them from being collected.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: The stage was set for the Patriots and their strategy of disruption.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: In the cities, particularly Boston, angry Patriot elites began mobilizing whatever physical power they could muster.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Like in Quebec, they again tapped into their personal networks – business clients for the merchant John Hancock; political clients for the politician Sam Adams.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: They were organized into what were essentially personal mobs, ready to riot on their patron’s command.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: In an age before modern policing, it wasn’t so difficult for riots to stop government policy execution.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Mobs barred people from paying taxes, attacked tax collectors and officers, and even burnt down the house of the Massachusetts Lieutenant Governor.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: As a result, nobody paid or collected the taxes, rendering the Parliamentary decision completely impotent.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: After a year, the establishment bowed to reality and repealed both taxes.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: The Stamp Act Riots showcased how Patriot disruption would work.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Through extra-ordinary political action and physical violence, colonists demonstrated that they could prevent establishment policy from being executed.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: That said, the Patriots won only because the British were completely unprepared – and the stakes were too high for them to surrender after one failure.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Like the Moderates, the Patriots had to ask themselves: what would they do to resist the next, inevitably more powerful attack?

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Patriot Disruption 2: Vanguardism

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Unlike the Moderates, the Patriots would develop a response to the problem of growing establishment power.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: And in doing so, they would become an early example for a new social movement grand strategy – Mass Agitation or Vanguardism.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: To understand vanguardism, we should first review what the colonists had been doing so far.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Earlier, we said that social movements revolve around two things: issues, which drive public participation, and organization, which converts this participation into power.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: From this, we can derive three grand strategies: one focusing on issues, one on organization, and one balanced between the two.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Let’s first look at the issue-heavy grand strategy, or ‘Spontaneous Uprising’.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: In a Spontaneous Uprising, activists focus on finding and deploying a hot-button issue that gets as many people as possible participating in the movement.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Nobody forces people to participate in the movement; nobody instructs participants what to do once in the movement.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: The whole movement is supported by pure amateurish enthusiasm, and one can’t expect enthusiastic amateurs to have the discipline or coordination required for effective work.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: So while Spontaneous Uprisings are extremely easy to set up, they tend to be very ineffective at producing power, and only win if they can attract a massive number of participants, or are facing a very weak establishment.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: The colonial resistance in Quebec and during the Stamp Act were examples of Spontaneous Uprisings.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: In both cases, the movement successfully got colonists so angry that they began resisting the imperial establishment in whatever way they saw fit: lobbying in Quebec, riots in Boston.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Both prevailed over an unprepared imperial establishment, but there was every indication that this grand strategy was reaching its limits.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: For one, the imperial establishment was getting prepared.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Parliament laid the legal groundwork by declaring its authority over the colonies, and eventually, it would enforce this by sending troops over, particularly to Boston.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: By mustering more of the state’s political and physical powers, the British hoped to set the bar for victory beyond what the colonists had been able to achieve so far.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Even without these measures, colonial power was already weakening.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: This is typical of Spontaneous Uprisings: since their success relies on using issues to whip up public enthusiasm, they tend to suffer massive attrition in the medium and long runs, as participants calm down, get exhausted or bored, and drop out.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Attrition was a particularly pressing problem for the Patriots, since their strategy of disruption, which carried serious physical and legal risks, demanded exceptionally high enthusiasm from participants.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: The initial shock of the Stamp Act helped get people up in arms, but now that the British were dragging things out, there was every chance that their intrusions would become ‘normalized’, and colonists would lose their enthusiasm for high-risk rioting.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: But in a way, attrition was only a serious problem because so far, the colonial resistance had let people freely decide when to participate in the movement, and what to do once in it.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: But what if the Patriots could change that, just a little? What if they could artificially encourage people to participate, or artificially raise the amount of power each participant contributed with their work? Then the Patriots would be able to sustain their power and hold their ground in a long-term contest against the imperial establishment.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: This is where vanguardism, as a grand strategy, comes in.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: In it, a movement establishes specialist organizations, known as ‘vanguards’, to structure and coordinate work in a way that boosts and sustains movement power.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: They can do this in three ways: first, vanguards can better refine, target and broadcast issues to the general public – also known as propaganda; second, they can impose structure on participants, increasing the efficiency of all aspects of work from recruitment to action; and finally, they can serve as a centralized command, observing the establishment and directing movement power to where it would be most impactful.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Unlike the famous Leninist vanguards, the Patriots didn’t need to organize from the ground up.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Instead, Patriot activists exploited their position as local elites to hijack colonial institutions and repurpose them as vanguards.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: All in all, the Patriots would end up relying on three major organizations: the Sons of Liberty, the Colonial Assemblies, and the Press.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: The Sons of Liberty were one of the few organizations that the Patriots created from scratch, having started out as a way to organize the private mobs in Boston.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: By inducting the elites who headed these mobs into a ‘secret society’ with set goals and codes of conduct, the Sons incentivized elites to deploy their power in ways that helped the movement, rather than for personal gain.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: On the other end of society, the Sons increased the efficiency of Patriot recruitment by lowering the risks or costs of participation.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: They offered an anonymous identity, which shielded Patriots from legal or social reprisals.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: They also offered a basic organizational template, which Patriots in other colonies could easily copy to set up their own local cells.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: These templates also standardized Patriot ideology and action across the various cells, minimizing disputes that could have arisen out of group differences.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Next were the Colonial Assemblies, chief among them the Massachusetts House of Representatives, and the Boston Town Meeting.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Patriots in these colonial institutions could both politically disrupt the Royal Governor and support the work of other Patriots as vanguards.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: They set up Committees of Correspondence to communicate, coordinate and share resistance intel with Patriots in other colonies.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: They provided political and legal cover for Patriot disruption and obstructed establishment crackdowns.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: And they also lent their political skills and influence to Patriot propaganda – most notably in creating slogans such as No Taxation without Representation.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Finally, we have the Press, which had been alienated from the imperial establishment ever since the Stamp Act.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: The Patriots further cemented this alliance by exploiting the media’s eternal desire for sensational and breaking news, which Patriots such as Benjamin Franklin and especially Sam Adams did to great effect.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: By taking over a local paper and converting it into a Patriot newswire, Adams could furnish the media with timely and dramatic propaganda, further enhanced with illustrations from Paul Revere.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: With this lure, the Patriots easily got the media to always broadcast the Patriot side of the story first, inevitably driving the public to sympathize with their movement.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: All three vanguards – the Sons of Liberty, the Colonial Assemblies, and the Press – were in place by the time the Stamp Act was repealed, and the Patriots would soon see the benefit from their contributions.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: But if Patriot vanguardism was so helpful, why didn’t the Moderates create their own versions?

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: The simple answer is that vanguards, like any organization, requires resources.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: The Moderates, blinkered by their optimistic assessment of the struggle, simply didn’t want to spend more on their movement, especially when they already had the London merchants to generate power.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: As a result, Moderate action throughout this period remained uncoordinated, dependent on individual enthusiasm, and often self-canceling.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: As such, the one major Moderate attempt at a united front, the Stamp Act Congress of 1765, predictably failed, as powerful New York and South Carolina Moderates refused to share their establishment connections, prioritizing their own gains over the welfare of the colonists as a whole.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Patriots vs Moderates: Townshend and Coercive Acts, 1767-1774

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Despite the imperial establishment’s failure in Quebec and now the Stamp Act, the stakes over imperial reform were still too high for them to give up.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: So, after a brief interval, which the British hoped would reduce colonial enthusiasm for resistance, Parliament passed the Townshend Acts in 1767, placing taxes on a new set of goods ranging from paper to glass to tea.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Contrary to British hopes, the Patriots responded by resuming their campaign of political and physical disruption.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: With their vanguards acting in support, the Patriots were not only able to sustain their resistance, but more importantly, they were able to keep up even as the British committed more power to the fight.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: The British sent troops into Boston; the Patriots sent mobs to fight them, leading to events such as the Boston Massacre and New York’s Battle of Golden Hill.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: The British dissolved the Massachusetts House; the Patriots established a Convention of Towns and ran the colony from there.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Years of vanguard work had created an expansive and powerful Patriot movement that the British, yet again, did not have the local resources to handle.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: And in being at the forefront of colonial resistance, the Patriots captured the imagination of other colonists.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: The time was ripe for the Patriots to further expand their movement, and it made sense to start with fellow Moderates, who shared similar attitudes towards British imperial reform.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: If the Patriots could get enough Moderates to join them, not only would their numbers increase, but they would also become the main voice for the entire colonial resistance, and the ones best positioned to impose change across the colonies.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: But was it even possible for Patriots to convert Moderates? After all, most Moderates could admit that Patriot disruption was effective, especially compared to their own efforts.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Nevertheless, their main concern was on the principles behind Patriot disruption, and its potential consequences to society.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Moderates worried that Patriot disruption would encourage political violence, force a break with the mother country, and ultimately leave the colonies as isolated, unstable communities vulnerable to domestic and foreign threats.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Simply doing more disruption wasn’t going to make Moderates any less wary of the Patriots.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: In response, some Patriots promoted a new disruption tactic: one without political violence and minimal rebelliousness, while still ensuring that imperial reform would be rendered unworkable.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: This was the boycott.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Boycotts seemed like a great Patriot answer to Moderate worries.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Aside from solving said worries, they would again render the Townshend taxes un-collectable.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Boycotting was also a familiar practice across the colonies: Northern merchants did it to keep out foreign imports, while Southern landowners used it to manage crop prices.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: What’s more, boycotting for the colonial cause also gave indebted elites a convenient reason to cut expenses without losing face!

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: But if the idea was good, the Patriots failed in the execution.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Moderate traders wouldn’t accept Patriot supervision over the boycotts, so the Patriots couldn’t use their vanguards to organize the action.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Instead, they would have to trust that Moderate traders would be enthusiastic enough to self-police and sustain the action for as long as needed.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: The results were disappointing.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: The boycott was only effective in Massachusetts, where strong Patriot vanguards could enforce the boycott.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Elsewhere, Moderate merchants immediately accused each other of cheating, and smaller landholders and traders ignored the boycott entirely.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Group disputes grew so disruptive that, had Parliament not again repealed most of the Townshend taxes in 1770, the boycott might well have collapsed from colonial infighting.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: To a few Patriots, the Townshend boycotts seemed to confirm that the Patriots and Moderates simply didn’t mix: there was no way the Patriots could accommodate Moderate sensibilities without compromising their own effectiveness as a movement.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Therefore, they returned to tried-and-tested methods of physical disruption, in particular against the only major Townshend tax remaining by 1773 – the tax on tea.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Most Patriots and Moderates had, in fact, already planned another continent-wide boycott of the incoming tea ships; but to a few Boston Patriots, the only real guarantee lay in destroying the product.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: So, in a surprise and surgical strike, the Bostonians boarded the ships, disposed of the tea, and left without triggering any further confrontation or collateral damage.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: As a tactical action, the Boston Tea Party represented the apex of Patriot disruption.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: In reality, the Tea Party turned out to be a Patriot own goal.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: The furious British responded with a dramatic escalation of power: under the Coercive Acts, the port of Boston was closed, the Massachusetts constitution was suspended, and colonial judicial rights were restricted – and the British would back this up with another troop reinforcement.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: The Patriots defiantly set up their own Massachusetts Provincial Government in response, but the reality was that establishment power had now far outstripped the Patriots’ capabilities, and to keep up, the movement needed the participation and help of the Moderates.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: There was no help.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: There were a few private donations, demonstrations of support, and other symbolic gestures.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Fear of what Britain might do to the other colonies also drove local elites to set up vanguard institutions in the Patriot style, mostly permanent Committees of Correspondence that could act as an alternative government should colonial legislatures be dissolved.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: But most of the colonies refused to act with Massachusetts against the Coercive Acts, not even in a general boycott.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: In the eyes of the Moderates who led these colonies, the Boston Patriots pretty much brought this on themselves.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Instead, Moderates proposed to invite all the North American colonies to a Continental Congress to discuss the potential for a joint boycott against the Coercive Acts.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: This idea was, in fact, a political poison pill – the Moderates knew that they still outnumbered the Patriots, and so intended to use the Congress to force the Patriots to accept and follow the Moderate lead from here on out.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: The Patriots couldn’t reject the Congress – after all, they were the ones asking for Moderate help.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: And so the Massachusetts Patriots, having just reached their apex a short while ago, traveled to the Congress in Philadelphia half-expecting to be completely defeated – not by the British, but by the Moderates.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Patriotism Dominant: The 1st Continental Congress, 1774

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: The First Continental Congress that opened in September 1774 was meant to be an overwhelmingly Moderate institution.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Most of the delegates from the 12 participating colonies were wealthy elites with strong desires for social stability and continued trade with Britain, and some states, notably New York, had deliberately diluted the Patriot influence within their delegation.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Philadelphia, the hosting city of the Congress, was a bastion of Moderate traders.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: So it speaks to the power of the Patriot movement that they still got the Congress to endorse and even go beyond the Patriot version of the boycott.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: In short, the Congress became a mini-demonstration of effective Patriot Vanguardism.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: First, the Patriots established a special message service between Boston and Philadelphia, ensuring that they, again, had the first take on developing events.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Immediately after the Congress began, Sam Adams used this service to spread propaganda regarding a British attack on Boston, coupled with news of brave colonial resistance.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Unsurprisingly, this ‘Powder Alarm’ helped generate a more pro-Patriot attitude amongst the delegates.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: The Patriots then hijacked the Congress by infiltrating the subcommittees responsible for reviewing the various boycott proposals.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Shrewdly, John Adams and his Massachusetts Patriots gave these tasks to allies from other colonies, avoiding Moderate suspicion in the process.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: As a result, the subcommittee ultimately recommended the Patriot version of the boycott, which proposed an immediate boycott on all British goods.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: The rest of the Congress accepted their decisions.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: With this subcommittee vanguard effectively setting the Congress’ agenda, the tables were turned, and the Patriots now forced Moderates to follow Patriot policy.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Delegates agreed to additionally ban American exports to Britain in a year’s time; they also endorsed community resolutions that took a hard-line stance towards British rule.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: But most importantly, the Congress agreed with Patriots that effective boycotts needed supervision and, as a result, created the ‘Continental Association’, where each local community would establish a committee to ensure compliance with the boycott.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: And here, not even the Patriots themselves could have fully appreciated what they had unleashed onto the colonists.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Compulsory Patriotism: The Continental Association, 1774-5

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: The establishment of the Continental Association marks the second transition in Patriot grand strategy, from the balanced strategy of Vanguardism to the organization-focused one of ‘Ideological Mobilization’.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Let’s quickly review the grand strategies again.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: In the issue-focused ‘Spontaneous Uprising’, the movement’s power comes entirely from the issue, and the enthusiasm it whips up amongst the public.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: In the balanced grand strategy of Vanguardism, the movement’s power still requires an issue and some public enthusiasm, but the effect of the two is enhanced by organizational work.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Now, in the organization-heavy strategy of Ideological Mobilization, the movement’s power comes entirely from organizational work: participants don’t choose what to do in a movement, and often can’t even choose whether to join or not.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Instead, the movement’s organizations assign work to the participant, much like a mini-bureaucracy or state, and it is this compulsory work that generates movement power.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Ideological Mobilization is most relevant when the movement is built around a fringe issue that can’t attract the public participation needed for victory.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: This was essentially where the Patriot movement had been ever since the Townshend Acts: to match the surging power of the British, the Patriots had asked for Moderate help, but that help either wasn’t coming or came with too many strings attached.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: But now, with the establishment of the Continental Association, the Patriots no longer needed to ask.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: The Association was the perfect vehicle for Patriot Ideological Mobilization.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Because the decision came from the Continental Congress, which claimed to represent the collective will of all colonists, every community had to set up a local Association branch.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Because the Patriots, thanks to their vanguards, were powerful and organized, they easily dominated most of the local branches.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: And because the Association had a mandate to supervise the boycott and stop any colonist from using British goods, this gave the local Associations immense power over public behavior and private life.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: In short, the Patriots, through the Associations, now enjoyed unprecedented power over the colonists living in the Thirteen Colonies.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: The Patriots soon abused this power to force colonists into their movement.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: They circled official petitions where all colonists had to publicly declare their support of the Patriot boycott.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: They set up supervising committees and town meetings which all colonists had to attend.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: They granted themselves huge powers to spy, search, and bully all suspected opponents.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: And at all points of this process, they made sure that the colonists were subject to an unrelenting stream of Patriot propaganda.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: By doing all this, the Patriots weren’t really trying to turn Moderates into enthusiastic Patriots.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Instead, what they wanted was for the colonists, whatever their real beliefs, to publicly act and work as if they were Patriots, and in doing so contribute positively to the Patriot movement.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: We can see this in action, when we briefly look at how the Patriots suppressed a major rival – the Loyalists.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Contrary to popular image, most Loyalists were actually ‘ultra-Moderates’, as in people who also disliked British imperial reform; in fact, many Loyalists were Moderate leaders.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Ultimately, however, Loyalists chose distant British rule over what they saw as local Patriot tyranny.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Stung by the Continental Congress and the shock defeat of the Moderates, Loyalists began setting up their own vanguardist counter-movement, intending to use Patriot methods against their own creators.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: A Loyalist movement could have been a strong force.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Modern scholars estimate that 15% of colonists within the Thirteen Colonies were Loyalists, among them elites who had extensive networks and resources.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: They had enthusiastic allies in the press, the legislatures, and amongst the Highland Scottish colonists.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: The British establishment did what it could to support them.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Yet the Loyalists would not be given the chance to live up to their potential.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Immediately, the Patriots launched a continent-wide crackdown against Loyalists.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Local Associations set up loyalty tests and spy networks to create an atmosphere of constant surveillance.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: They rooted out and punished anybody who was suspected of anti-Patriot behavior, sometimes through physical or psychological torture, but mostly through ‘Civil Excommunication’, in which other colonists were banned from interacting with them.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Patriot propaganda encouraged colonists to view Loyalists as slaves and traitors to their neighbors.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: These Patriot actions made a mockery out of their supposed devotion to Locke, but they effectively neutered the Loyalist movement.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Known Loyalist elites and vanguards were harassed out of their communities and lost the ability to organize movements.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Hidden Loyalists were forced to act in secret and on a small scale, which greatly limited their ability to generate significant power.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: And Loyalist sympathizers amongst the public would, out of fear of punishment, disguise themselves as Patriots and work to destroy what they actually believed in.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: As a result, the Loyalist movement never posed a major challenge to the Patriots, and oftentimes would exist only when large British forces were nearby.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: If Patriot Ideological Mobilization was strong enough to effectively silence the Loyalist segment of the colonial population, then there really was no hope for the miniscule and beleaguered representatives of the British imperial establishment.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: By early 1775, the American Revolution was essentially complete in the Thirteen Colonies: now with the willing and unwilling support of most colonists, the Patriots easily overpowered whatever imperial power remained.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: The colonial militia and government stopped obeying British orders.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Royal Governors fled to nearby warships and Royal forts were taken by storm.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: The Patriots were now free to impose whatever change they wanted, and after the Battle of Lexington and Thomas Paine’s Common Sense, that change would turn out to be full independence.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: The only way the British could possibly overpower the movement now was by sending over a massive military force, and their decision to do that set the stage for the American Revolutionary War.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Movement Failure: Canada

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: How could the British imperial establishment let a colonial dispute spiral so catastrophically out of control? Well, as we have seen, the British repeatedly committed the cardinal sin of movement suppression: they responded to each strengthening of colonial power with proportionate, rather than overwhelming force.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Even on the eve of Lexington, when the colonies were basically independent, General Gage in Boston still only had 3 thousand troops to suppress the Patriots, rather than the 20 thousand he had requested.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: And if those 20 thousand troops had arrived in Boston immediately after the Stamp Act Riots, the Patriot movement would have been squashed as soon as it had begun.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: These failures occurred because the British establishment did not want to pay for so many troops, and – surprise! – they genuinely believed that such actions would have been tyrannical.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: The Patriots rarely fell victim to such concerns, especially when suppressing the Loyalists, and that gave them an advantage over their enemies.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: There was another way to defeat the colonial movement that didn’t involve force.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Local elites were by far the most valuable supporters of the colonial resistance, providing the resources, networks, and social acceptance that the movement would otherwise have taken years to build up.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: That’s why autocrats have often placed local elites under close establishment watch, like how the French moved their nobility to Versailles.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: A few establishment figures proposed something similar for American elites, but this was always seen as a fringe and un-British policy.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Which brings us to Canada.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: The British establishment largely failed to keep the colonial Anglo elite on their side, but with Quebec, the sheer cultural differences between ruler and ruled made it obvious that the British needed to adopt a strategy of cooptation, and convince the locals to stick with British rule.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: The Quebec Act of 1774, which granted religious tolerance and some acceptance of French law within the province, made British rule far more agreeable to the Quebecois elite, especially compared with the alternative, which was rule by the Anglo colonists that had so recently tried to destroy them.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: And so, despite repeated appeals by the Continental Congresses and even military invasion, Quebec stuck with the British.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Nova Scotia showcased another form of elite cooptation.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: The colony was about the same size as Georgia, and furthermore, half its population was from rebellious New England.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Throughout the period of the American Revolution, the colony also suffered from major political instability, largely caused by the royal Governor’s attempt to take over nearby Prince Edward Island and sell it to the Nova Scotian elite.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: But such corruption kept the elite close to the imperial establishment, which meant that unlike Georgia, Nova Scotia would reject the Continental Association, even at the risk of being boycotted by the other colonies.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: These elite cooptation tactics were not perfect or foolproof: attempts to bribe elites in Virginia and New York generally just drove the losing side to support the colonial resistance.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: But given the importance of elites to the colonial movement, anything that could temporarily reduce their anger towards Britain was helpful, at least until the establishment position could be shored up by the two ultimate guarantors of stability, which were British troops and Loyalist refugees.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Conclusion

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: In terms of the strategy of protest and revolution, the American Revolution was extremely innovative, even compared to its more influential peers like the French Revolution.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: In the attempt to overcome colonial division and match the power of the British, the colonial resistance, especially its radical Patriot wing, moved from a Spontaneous Uprising based on pure enthusiasm, to a balanced strategy of Vanguardism and finally, to the proto-government of Ideological Mobilization.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: In doing so, the Patriots demonstrated that revolutions could be ‘made’, and that even fringe radical ideologies had a shot at seizing power.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: However, we must also acknowledge that the colonial movement was playing on ‘Very Easy’ mode.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Its activists and leaders were colonial elites, who had the resources, networks, and social status to build a movement at a comparatively low cost.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Its opponent was the British establishment, who, rather than being the ‘tyrants’ of Patriot propaganda, actually responded extremely complacently to colonial unrest.

来源: Strategy of Protest and Revolution 3: The American Revolution (1763-1775) [16/4/2021]
内容: Nevertheless, the American Revolution was in many ways an organizational triumph, and many future movements would spend much blood and treasure trying to replicate its effects.

来源: The Russian Bolshevik Revolution (Mar-Nov 1917) | Strategy of Protest and Revolution 4.5 [13/4/2023]
内容: Introduction

来源: The Russian Bolshevik Revolution (Mar-Nov 1917) | Strategy of Protest and Revolution 4.5 [13/4/2023]
内容: Russia went through 2 revolutions in 1917.

来源: The Russian Bolshevik Revolution (Mar-Nov 1917) | Strategy of Protest and Revolution 4.5 [13/4/2023]
内容: First, the February Revolution overthrew Czarist autocracy for a liberal Provisional Government; then, the October Revolution overthrew the Provisional Government for a socialist regime that would later become the Soviet Union.

来源: The Russian Bolshevik Revolution (Mar-Nov 1917) | Strategy of Protest and Revolution 4.5 [13/4/2023]
内容: Between these 2 revolutions, the Bolsheviks, led by Lenin, went from being a small group, to one that could take over Russia’s capital of Petrograd.

来源: The Russian Bolshevik Revolution (Mar-Nov 1917) | Strategy of Protest and Revolution 4.5 [13/4/2023]
内容: How did Lenin pull this off?

来源: The Russian Bolshevik Revolution (Mar-Nov 1917) | Strategy of Protest and Revolution 4.5 [13/4/2023]
内容: Let’s first review what social movements are about.

来源: The Russian Bolshevik Revolution (Mar-Nov 1917) | Strategy of Protest and Revolution 4.5 [13/4/2023]
内容: A ‘social movement’ harnesses the collective power of ordinary people to impose change upon society.

来源: The Russian Bolshevik Revolution (Mar-Nov 1917) | Strategy of Protest and Revolution 4.5 [13/4/2023]
内容: In this, it is resisted by an ‘establishment’ that represents existing interests, and can use the powers of the state – particularly those related to coercion and violence – to maintain said interests.

来源: The Russian Bolshevik Revolution (Mar-Nov 1917) | Strategy of Protest and Revolution 4.5 [13/4/2023]
内容: Against this, movements do 2 things.

来源: The Russian Bolshevik Revolution (Mar-Nov 1917) | Strategy of Protest and Revolution 4.5 [13/4/2023]
内容: First, they raise ‘issues’ that encourage the public to participate in the movement; second, they create ‘organizations’ that turn this participation into power: physical, political, and more.

来源: The Russian Bolshevik Revolution (Mar-Nov 1917) | Strategy of Protest and Revolution 4.5 [13/4/2023]
内容: Power is what a movement uses to achieve change: either by getting the establishment to negotiate, or by overpowering it entirely in a revolution.

来源: The Russian Bolshevik Revolution (Mar-Nov 1917) | Strategy of Protest and Revolution 4.5 [13/4/2023]
内容: On the surface, Russia in 1917 was fertile ground for a ‘socialist’ movement based around the interests of the lower classes.

来源: The Russian Bolshevik Revolution (Mar-Nov 1917) | Strategy of Protest and Revolution 4.5 [13/4/2023]
内容: Decades of minimal socioeconomic reform had created huge resentments amongst the poor: rural peasants were crushed by unrepayable debt, while urban workers slaved in miserable and humiliating conditions.

来源: The Russian Bolshevik Revolution (Mar-Nov 1917) | Strategy of Protest and Revolution 4.5 [13/4/2023]
内容: On top of this, Russia’s participation in World War One had ended German imports and disrupted civilian logistics, resulting in soaring inflation, collapsing living conditions and an explosion in political discontent.

来源: The Russian Bolshevik Revolution (Mar-Nov 1917) | Strategy of Protest and Revolution 4.5 [13/4/2023]
内容: Despite this, serious obstacles still stood in the way of socialist success.

来源: The Russian Bolshevik Revolution (Mar-Nov 1917) | Strategy of Protest and Revolution 4.5 [13/4/2023]
内容: Problem & Issue 1: Socialism in Russia

来源: The Russian Bolshevik Revolution (Mar-Nov 1917) | Strategy of Protest and Revolution 4.5 [13/4/2023]
内容: The first obstacle to socialist success was establishment state power, especially the Russian secret police with its extensive monitoring and infiltration capabilities.

来源: The Russian Bolshevik Revolution (Mar-Nov 1917) | Strategy of Protest and Revolution 4.5 [13/4/2023]
内容: The Bolsheviks developed several responses to state suppression, as we’ll see later, but this was ultimately not enough and by 1917, the movement had been neutralized throughout Russia.

来源: The Russian Bolshevik Revolution (Mar-Nov 1917) | Strategy of Protest and Revolution 4.5 [13/4/2023]
内容: Still, evading state power was seen mainly as a matter of practical execution; and it therefore took a back seat to the task of formulating an actual movement strategy.

来源: The Russian Bolshevik Revolution (Mar-Nov 1917) | Strategy of Protest and Revolution 4.5 [13/4/2023]
内容: Which brings us to the second and far more fundamental obstacle: socialism’s unpopularity in 1917 Russia.

来源: The Russian Bolshevik Revolution (Mar-Nov 1917) | Strategy of Protest and Revolution 4.5 [13/4/2023]
内容: While many Russians were sick of the Czarist establishment, that didn’t mean that they saw socialism as the solution.
